The new branch table is structurally present, but its retained cardinality labels and URI-qualified predicate do not define the same multiplicity domain; see SARIFV11-S2.
Produced goldens still cannot derive a single branch for mixed primary-role entries with and without URIs because the retained and new cardinality terms diverge.

The branch is expressly host-owned, but its reference to the D9-bearing output path needs an explicit source-consistent classification so projection validation is not read as choosing D9/exit; see SARIFV11-S3.

shouldFix.title: The multiple-primary branch invokes the exact D9 output-failure path without classifying the check as a post-commit serialization failure
detail: validationBeforePlacement counts qualifying primaries before placementRule. Its multiple branch says: 'Refuse the projection through the existing host-owned required-output-failure path.'

That path is not a generic refusal bucket. requiredOutputFailure and the exact permitted file-01 lines 92-99 restrict it to a post-commit required serialization/atomic-write operation failure, yielding operational-failed / OUTPUT.SERIALIZATION_FAILED / exit 4 while preserving an already-committed Run.

Multiple URI-bearing primary candidates are a hostLocationList mapping/precondition defect detected before placement. They may be intended as a validation phase of the host's post-commit serialization operation, but v11 does not say that and cites no separate D9-owner classification.

Without that classification, the text can be read either as an ordinary instance of the existing serializer failure or as a newly minted trigger for the existing D9 code/exit. The full public outcome is therefore underspecified even though the host, not a component, owns the branch.
shouldFix.impact: A future produced case cannot tell whether multiple primaries are a non-D9 mapping refusal or the existing post-commit serialization failure with its public code and exit.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: State explicitly that validationBeforePlacement runs inside the existing post-commit required serialization operation and that multiple qualifying primaries make that operation fail under the already-cited golden, or choose the same non-failing native-array suppression used by the zero branch. Do not create a new code, exit, or D-096 grant.

shouldFix.title: The retained cardinality labels and the new validation predicate disagree on what counts as multiple primaries
detail: The retained cardinality object says multiplePrimaries 'refuses' without qualifying on URI presence. The new predicate counts only entries that have both role=primary and a locationUri.

With two role=primary entries but a URI on only one, the retained label says multiple primaries while validationBeforePlacement counts exactly one and proceeds. With two primary-role entries and no URIs, the retained label still says multiple while the new table takes the zero branch.
The new table may intend 'primary' everywhere to mean a URI-bearing qualifying primary, but v11 adds rather than replaces the older unqualified members, so that equivalence is not stated.
shouldFix.impact: A future produced native-location golden cannot select one branch for mixed URI/non-URI primary-role entries.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Define the retained cardinality members explicitly in terms of qualifying primaries under the new predicate, or replace them with the validationBeforePlacement table so one count domain governs every branch.
